sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests who decides if a foreign conviction matches a U.S. crime definition. the side that brought the case argues judges must resolve ambiguity in his favor. The government argues juries decide factual questions about the conviction.

paragraphs: This case determines who decides if a foreign conviction matches a U.S. crime definition. It affects how courts handle ambiguous foreign criminal records. It shapes the balance between judicial interpretation and jury fact-finding in immigration cases.
